# Step 2.123: team fouls that reset each half or once a game

## Builder one: the engine and core (layer 1)

**What exists.** The engine's rules gain `teamFoulsReset` (`'period' | 'half' | 'game'`), absent being each period (`packages/sports/src/basketball/live.ts`: the type, `TEAM_FOULS_RESETS`, `foulWindow`, the count in `derive`, kept by `checkRules` when given and refused when wrong). `periodFouls`, the bonus and the double bonus follow the window. Overtime continues the last regulation window's count: S-114, decided for you (P7 is silent; the engine already did this for each period). `engineRulesOf` carries the season's choice only when it counts differently from each period (once a game, or each half with quarters), like the other optional rules (T-420); `trackerEngineRulesOf` drops it, since a game brought over was counted each period. A started game keeps its rules (S-1, through `withCurrentRules`, tested). The note in `engine-rules.ts` is corrected (M8, L8). The platform's command shape (`PlatformRules` in `packages/contracts/src/live-stats.ts`) takes it; the Al-Hadi shape still refuses it. P7 §1 and T6 (T-128's section) are corrected; rows in `decisions-pending/S-114.md` and `T-420.md`. No migration.

**Tests.** New `tests/live-stats-team-fouls-reset.test.mjs` (9): the audit's example first (4 in Q1, 3 in Q2, by the half: 7 and the bonus in Q2; each period: 3, none), Q3 starting again, double bonus, once a game, overtime for each reset, undo/redo/unfoul, a foul moved back across a period line (by a period change and by editing the play's period, as a grid correction does), the format keeping and refusing the field, the device engine agreeing, and the random-plays test (ten seeds, quarters and halves, 300 random commands each: "each period" absent and present give the same derived game after every command and the same state but for the field). Also `engine-rules.test.ts` (+4, and the "custom" case now expects `teamFoulsReset: 'half'`, which is the admin's value carried) and `live-stats.test.ts` (+1).

**Broken by hand.** `foulWindow`'s half returning the period: 5 engine tests failed; its once-a-game returning the period: 2 failed; its default read as 'half': the random test and 3 more failed; `teamFoulsResetOf` dropping 'half': 4 core tests failed. Each put back.

**Run.** Before: `tests/live-stats-*.test.mjs` 143 of 143; vitest on sports, games and contracts 714 in 72 files. After, with no existing engine or live-stats test file edited: the same 143 of 143 (the new file apart); vitest on core, contracts, sports and `tracker-commands.test.ts` 2306 in 226 files; `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (442 of 442) pass.

**Left for layer 2.** The tracker's badge and horn already read `periodFouls` (`apps/web/src/features/tracker/scoring-view.ts` line 289), so they follow, but their words may still say "this period"; the public page and the live snapshot should be checked the same way. Season settings still hold the choice back (`teamFoulsResetFor` in `apps/web/src/features/season-settings/season-parts.ts` forces each period with quarters and turns once a game into each half with halves, step 2.47's rule): offer each half with quarters and once a game, and the game-format panel likewise. A browser test (quarters by the half: 7 fouls, the badge and the horn in Q2, on the public page too). The pinned lists for anything new.

**What I distrust.** No season can reach the engine with a value that matters until the settings let one (so nothing in the product shows it yet). A season changed while a game is live keeps the old count for that game by design (S-1); the admin may not expect it. The random test draws from the commands the engine knows today; a new command type is not in it.

**Lines in other lanes' folders.** Lane 2.65's `packages/core/src/modules/games`: `engine-rules.ts` (the header note, lines 9 to 15; `trackerEngineRulesOf` and the new `teamFoulsResetOf`, lines 31 to 56; one line in `engineRulesOf`, line 82) and `engine-rules.test.ts` (one import, three lines in "carries every value the admin set", and a new block at the end). `apply-plays.ts` is not touched.
